state.target_passage: I adopt the bough-annotation rule and the 02:00 graduated-cylinder procedure; without that winter secondary read a snowpack that hoards and later releases four millimetres overnight would surface as a phantom 0.4 mm/hr rate in the hourly log, exactly the kind of artifact your pruning note is meant to eliminate. For the pressure variable you listed but have not yet instrumented, each site will carry a sealed aneroid module (0.1 hPa resolution) calibrated monthly against a NIST-traceable portable barometer, and every reading is reduced to mean-sea level using the site's surveyed elevation and a temperature-corrected lapse rate before the weekly comparison column is populated. The failure this guards against is mundane but diagnostic: if Site 3, sitting eighteen metres above Site 1, simply logs raw station pressure and the compiler forgets the MSL correction, the bulletin shows a persistent ≈1.5 hPa "high" at Site 3 that mimics a blocked-ridge signature and poisons the cross-site coherence check. I therefore require that any inter-site pressure spread exceeding 0.5 hPa after MSL reduction triggers an automatic elevation-recording audit—a repeat GPS survey of the affected site—rather than a silent averaging across the six columns.
